## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō chūfēn shuō jīng* (T498) is a two-fascicle sūtra translated by the Sòng Indian monk [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) Shīhù (*Dānapāla*; d. 1017 CE). The title's *chūfēn* 初分 refers to the "first division" — possibly Sanskrit *prathamabhāga* — of a larger Indic compilation.

**Abstract**

Shīhù was one of the three principal Indian monks at the Sòng *Yìjīng yuàn* (with [天息災](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E6%81%AF%E7%81%BD) Tiānxīzāi/[法賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%B3%A2) Fǎxián and [法天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E5%A4%A9) Fǎtiān/Dharmadeva), arriving in Cháng'ān in 980 CE. He was prolific and produced about 110 translations. This text concerns the early sections of an Indic compilation on the Buddha's life and teaching career; the precise *Vorlage* is not fully identified. Translation is dated to Shīhù's productive period (989–1017 CE).
